sources.content: Superseded transport decoder policy: each data frame ends a text record, and an empty frame closes the pending record. This policy was valid only before the framed-record protocol cutover at 09:00 UTC.

The framed log reader carries up to three unfinished UTF-8 bytes between data frames belonging to one record. An empty heartbeat frame neither flushes those bytes nor ends the record. Only the explicit record_end flag closes the text record; an incomplete character at that flag is a decoding error. Fixture evidence: the three bytes of the euro character split across two data frames with an intervening heartbeat decode to one character.

In the frame-records experiment, every transport frame is a complete record. Reject a character split across frames and treat an empty frame as an empty completed record. This experiment is confined to the lantern-experiment worktree and experiment/frame-records branch.
The operations dashboard subtracts heartbeat frame headers from the payload-byte chart and samples that chart every thirty seconds. This display accounting does not define decoder boundaries.

cases.description: Keep feature-branch binding-aware rename facts reusable across sessions without inheriting another branch from the same working tree or an unrelated teaching project.

sources.content: The main-branch prototype renamer replaces every token with the selected spelling and rejects a target spelling if it appears anywhere in the file. This remains the main-branch behavior; it is not the binding-aware feature branch behavior.

In fix/rename-bindings, rename edits are selected by resolved binding ID, not token spelling. A new local variable name conflicts only with a visible declaration in the value namespace at the affected references. A type alias or statement label with that spelling is not a value-namespace collision. A shadowed variable with the old spelling keeps its own binding ID and is not edited.

The feature branch computes all binding-aware rename edits and validates collisions before applying any edit. On a value-namespace collision, return the colliding declaration location and apply zero edits across the transaction.
The unrelated quill-demo is a teaching text editor: rename is literal whole-file replacement, including strings and comments. It accepts any destination spelling and has no binding resolver.
The feature branch import formatter keeps relative imports after package imports and preserves comments attached to each group. Import formatting has no effect on rename collision lookup.

cases.description: An explicit correction changes how nonexistent local times are resolved; later current recall and an earlier as-of recall must produce different answers with exact revision provenance.

sources.content: Daybridge gap rule revision 1: when a requested local time does not exist, scan forward to the first representable local minute. In the synthetic zone where 02:00 through 02:59:59 is missing, a 02:17 request resolves to 03:00. For an overlap, choose the occurrence with the earlier UTC instant.

Correction to Daybridge gap rule, effective 10:00 UTC: shift a nonexistent wall time forward by the exact width of the offset gap, preserving its displacement into the gap. In the synthetic one-hour jump from 02:00 to 03:00, 02:17 resolves to 03:17, not 03:00. Overlap resolution is unchanged: choose the occurrence with the earlier UTC instant. This is provider-local decision lineage gap-rule revision 2; it supersedes revision 1 for current use.

The schedule preview localizes weekday abbreviations using the selected UI locale and falls back to numeric month/day labels when a translation is absent. Label fallback never chooses a schedule instant.

sources.content: Prism inline diagnostic protocol revision 1 measures zero-based columns in Unicode scalar values. In the exact line A🧭Z, the Z starts at column 2. A literal tab counts as one scalar; these are protocol offsets, not visual cells.

Correction effective 10:00 UTC: Prism inline diagnostic columns are zero-based UTF-16 code-unit offsets. In A🧭Z, A consumes one unit and the compass character consumes two, so Z starts at column 3. A literal tab consumes one code unit regardless of editor tab width. Scalar counts and UTF-8 byte offsets are not this protocol.

The isolated byte-columns prototype addresses UTF-8 bytes. In A🧭Z, Z starts at byte 5. This wire format belongs only to the prism-byte-prototype worktree and is not a revision of the primary diagnostic protocol.
The diagnostic panel sorts severity groups as error, warning, note and keeps arrival order within a group. This sorting does not alter protocol positions.

cases.description: A useful crash-safe download decision must survive actual host/provider process replacement and duplicate canonical replay without reviving the retired resume rule or leaking an experiment.

sources.content: Retired mirror resume policy: use the current partial-file length as the next Range offset and keep those bytes when the server changes its ETag. This policy expired when durable sidecar checkpoints were introduced at 09:00 UTC.

The current mirror commits a checkpoint by syncing appended data before atomically replacing the sidecar containing committed_length and the object ETag. On reopen, truncate any data beyond committed_length before issuing a Range request at that committed length. If the response ETag differs from the checkpoint ETag, discard both partial bytes and the sidecar and start at offset zero. Fixture evidence: a file with 8192 bytes and a sidecar committing 6144 resumes at 6144 after truncation, not at 8192.
The no-sidecar experiment always streams from byte zero into a fresh temporary file and never attempts a Range request. It is confined to the harbor-direct-stream worktree.
The download progress display refreshes after each 256 KiB of received network data. The display counter includes bytes that are not yet in a committed checkpoint and cannot choose a resume offset.

sources.content: Mosaic publication rule revision 1: publish the next index first, then rename the generated chunk files into place. A reader may retry an index-listed chunk that is temporarily absent. This rule applied only before the atomic-release correction at 10:00 UTC.

Corrected Mosaic atomic-release rule: finish and sync each temporary chunk, rename all chunks to their immutable final names, and sync their parent directory before atomically replacing the published index. Keep the previous published index usable until the replacement index is durable. An interrupted build must leave readers on the old complete release, never on an index naming missing chunks.

Mosaic intermediate-cache entries are identified by normalized source path plus transform version. Changing the transform version invalidates the cached result even when source bytes and modification time are unchanged. Publication-order corrections do not change this key rule.

The live-index preview branch publishes each generated asset immediately and intentionally exposes a partially updated preview. That behavior belongs only to the mosaic-preview worktree and does not define production release publication.
The development banner prints the source-file count with a thin-space thousands separator. This count is presentation metadata and neither a release generation nor a cache key.
